candidates.notes: Source name: Mount Chinguacousy — Brampton.
Source name: Adanac Ski Hill — Sault Ste. Marie. PDF locality corrected: Adanac is in Greater Sudbury, not Sault Ste. Marie.
Source name: Antoine Mountain — Kenora. PDF locality corrected: Antoine Mountain is near Mattawa, not Kenora.
Source name: Batawa Ski Hill — near Trenton.

Source name: Mount Dufour — Thunder Bay. PDF locality corrected: Mount Dufour is in Elliot Lake, not Thunder Bay.
Source name: Mount Jamieson — Timmins.
Source name: Kamiskotia Snow Resort — Timmins. Kamiskotia is the former name of the same hill separately listed by the PDF as Mount Jamieson; it is not a second resort.
Source name: Uplands Ski Club — North Bay. PDF identity/locality corrected: the public Uplands Ski Centre is in Vaughan, not North Bay.
Source name: Trestle Ridge (Nordica) — Sudbury area. PDF locality corrected: Trestle Ridge, formerly Nordica, is at Terrace Bay, not near Sudbury.

candidates.officialIdentity: Centennial Park Ski and Snowboard Centre
candidates.notes: Source name: Centennial Park (Windsor). The PDF locality is erroneous. Windsor's Centennial Park is not this former downhill facility; Toronto permanently ceased ski/snowboard operations at Centennial Park after the 2021–22 season.

Source name: Devil's Elbow Ski Club (Barrie area). The PDF locality is erroneous. The former Devil's Elbow near Bethany reopened under the Bethany Ski Resort identity; the old name should not be added as a separate resort.

Source name: Old Smokey Ski Hill (Huntsville). Historical Huntsville-area hill; no current operator, lift tickets, operating plan, or official downhill web presence could be verified as of August 2026.
Source name: Skyloft Ski Area (Caledon). The PDF locality is erroneous: Skyloft was in the Uxbridge ski cluster, not Caledon. It has no current operator or public downhill operation.

Source name: Talisman Resort (Kimberley). The resort property has had non-ski redevelopment activity, but lift-served public downhill skiing remains closed and no ski operator or ticket sales were verified.

Source name: Red Mountain Resort — Rossland. The 2026/27 season-pass sale is current first-party evidence of continuing public downhill operation. No duplicate was found in an authored feelzlike region; the Powder Highway region currently contains Revelstoke, Kicking Horse, Fernie, Whitewater, Kimberley and Panorama.

Source name: Manning Park Resort — near Hope. The operator advertises 2026/27 season passes. The source's 'near Hope' is a travel description; the ski area is in Manning Park and that is the more accurate locality label.
Source name: Shames Mountain — Terrace. My Mountain Co-op is the operator identity; Shames Mountain remains the public-facing ski-area name.

Source name: Powder King Mountain Resort — Mackenzie. Operational-risk flag resolved: the official winter page says the 2025/26 season concluded and explicitly anticipates 'next season.' A sale or ownership dispute is not itself a closure.

Source name: Hemlock (Sasquatch Mountain Resort) — Agassiz. Duplicate/rename check resolved in favour of the current name: Hemlock Valley Resort is the former name, not a second hill. The reduced 2025/26 schedule does not fail the public-operation test because the operator is selling 2026/27 season passes.
Source name: Castle Mountain Resort — Pincher Creek/Westcastle Valley. No match in the authored Banff/Lake Louise, Canmore or Jasper regions.
Source name: Asessippi Ski Area & Resort — near Inglis/Russell. Public winter tickets, rentals and lessons are offered by the operator.
Source name: Mystery Mountain Winter Park — Thompson. The operator's current site advertises lift tickets, rentals and downhill events.
Source name: Holiday Mountain Resort — La Rivière. The current operator presents public lift-served skiing and snowboarding at La Rivière.

Source name: Stony Mountain Ski Area. Explicit exclusion. The source reports closure since the 2024/25 season, and the nominal official site supplies no dated 2026/27 reopening, tickets or operating calendar. Fail-closed pending a current operator announcement.
Source name: Mount Agassiz Ski Resort. Explicit exclusion. Parks Canada treats Mount Agassiz as historic infrastructure; there is no current ski operator or official resort URL.

Source name: Table Mountain — near Battleford. Use the Regional Park identity and its official social page. The canadaDirectory value https://www.tablemountain.ca is not accepted: it now identifies an unrelated New Brunswick hill and is a link-rot/domain-collision risk.
Source name: Duck Mountain Ski Area — Kamsack. The operator's current public ticket and ski-school pages establish public downhill use.
Source name: Wapiti Valley Ski Resort. The regional park is northeast of Melfort; Melfort is the nearest useful consumer locality.

Source name: Blackstrap Ski Hill. Explicit exclusion. Blackstrap Provincial Park remains open, but its current official activity listing has no alpine/downhill operation; the former ski hill is closed. Cross-country use does not qualify.

Source name: Owl's Head. Public seasonal lift-served ski area. The official site identifies Owl’s Head at its Mansonville address and continues to publish alpine-ski conditions, passes, packages, lessons, and rentals, including 2026-27 products.

Source name: Mont Orford. Public seasonal downhill ski area operated by the Corporation Ski & Golf Mont-Orford. Its official site publishes alpine-ski passes, day rates, conditions, lift status, and trail status.

Source name: Mont Grand-Fonds. Public seasonal alpine ski area. The official site publishes live alpine status, public lift tickets, and 2026-27 terms and season products; it states a 735-m summit and 335-m vertical.

Source name: Massif du Sud. Public seasonal lift-served ski area. The operator continues to sell public day tickets and season passes and describes its maintained downhill trail network on the official site.

Source name: Val Saint-Côme. Public seasonal ski area. The official site records the 2025-26 season and continues to provide alpine skiing, live conditions, public ticket sales, lessons, and equipment rental.
Source name: Stoneham. Public seasonal lift-served ski area. The official site publishes day and evening downhill conditions, trail and lift status, winter services, and public products.

Source name: Le Relais. Public seasonal ski area. Its official mountain and winter pages identify downhill skiing and snowboarding and publish 33 day trails, 27 night trails, conditions, rates, lessons, and rentals.

Source name: Tremblant. Already published in the live Laurentians region as Tremblant. The official resort remains a public outdoor downhill operation; this source-document exclusion must not create a duplicate catalogue entry. Keep the existing live record; do not add a second Tremblant record.

Source name: Mont Sutton. Already published in the live Eastern Townships region. The official site continues to advertise public downhill skiing; the 840-m value is the live catalogue's lift-served top rather than the higher natural summit. Keep the existing live record; do not add a second Mont Sutton record.

Source name: Bromont. Already published as Ski Bromont in the live Eastern Townships region. Its canonical official domain continues to advertise public downhill and night skiing. Keep the existing live Ski Bromont record; treat PDF shorthand 'Bromont' as the same area.

Source name: Le Massif. Already published in the live Charlevoix region. The official site continues to publish public winter mountain products and conditions and describes a 770-m lift-served vertical. Keep the existing live record; do not add a second Le Massif record.

Source name: Mont-Sainte-Anne. Already published in the live Charlevoix region. The official mountain domain continues to identify the public ski area and publish winter conditions and products. Keep the existing live record; do not add a second Mont-Sainte-Anne record.
Source name: Crabbe Mountain. Seasonal public alpine ski area; the official site identifies the ski resort, publishes lift-ticket/pass products and 2026 operating information.
Source name: Poley Mountain. Seasonal public ski hill; the official site was updated on 2026-08-26 and advertises 2026-27 winter ski season passes, day tickets, rentals, and public winter operations.

Source name: Sugarloaf Provincial Park. Public provincial-park alpine skiing remains advertised on the park's official winter page, including downhill skiing, lifts, snow conditions, and public tickets.

Source name: Mont Farlagne. The operating ski hill formerly catalogued as Mont Farlagne now presents itself officially as Républik Nature. Its ski page, modified 2026-05-20, advertises maintained alpine runs, woods terrain, tickets, rentals, hours, and live run status. Do not create a separate Mont Farlagne entity; use Républik Nature as the canonical identity and retain Mont Farlagne as an alias.
Source name: Ski Wentworth. Seasonal public lift-served ski area with official downhill trail, ticket, season-pass, lesson, rental, and conditions information.
Source name: Ski Martock. Seasonal public outdoor ski area whose official site continues to publish downhill tickets, passes, rentals, lessons, trail maps, and snow reporting.

Source name: Cape Smokey (Ski Cape Smokey). Public seasonal alpine skiing is an official Cape Smokey activity; the operator publishes ski/snowboard information, winter lift tickets, rentals, and mountain conditions.

Source name: Ski Ben Eoin. Community-operated public alpine hill. The official site, modified in May 2026, identifies active skiing and snowboarding and publishes tickets, passes, programs, and hill status.

Source name: White Hills Resort. The official site records completion of the 2025-26 winter season, describes 27 downhill trails, publishes public tickets/passes, and says the area will return next winter. Seasonal closure in August is not a resort closure.

Source name: Smokey Mountain Ski Club. Public community ski club with lift-served alpine terrain. The club's official web identity and official social channel continued to publish operations and public access information for the 2025-26 season. The official website intermittently returns an access-control page to automated clients; do not replace its domain based on that behavior.

Source name: Marble Mountain. Fail-closed for catalogue admission. The official site confirms the resort identity and a completed seasonal operation, but at the research cutoff it does not resolve the source document's material continuity warning: only one of three chairlifts was reported operating in November 2025 amid repeated unsuccessful government divestment attempts. A normal 2026-27 multi-chair public downhill plan was not found on an official source. Exclude from live operating inventory until current official evidence explicitly confirms a viable 2026-27 public downhill season and lift plan.
